# ADR 0001: Training data, architecture and engine stack

Date: 2026-10-13
Status: accepted

## Context

The model has to be small enough to train on one RTX 3060 Ti (8 GB) and to run in a browser tab, yet
behave well enough that what it does inside is worth watching. A model that writes nonsense has nothing
to show. The engine is written from scratch in Rust, so every architectural choice is code I write.

## Decision

**Data: TinyStories** (Eldan & Li, 2023): ~2.1M short stories in simple English, generated by GPT-3.5/4,
built so that models with 1–30M parameters still write fluent, coherent text. Licence (checked in M1):
**CDLA-Sharing-1.0**. Trained models are
"Results" under that licence and carry no obligations; only redistributing the data itself must keep
the licence.

Rejected:
- arXiv astro-ph titles from Night Sky Digest: ~51k titles is under a million tokens, so a small model
  overfits, and visitors can't read astro jargon in a visualization. Possible later as a fine-tune.
- Character-level text (e.g. Shakespeare): attention between single characters means nothing to a viewer.

**Tokenizer:** byte-level BPE, vocabulary 4096, trained on TinyStories. Small vocabulary keeps the
embedding table and the logit layer small; on this simple English most words are one token.

**Architecture: Llama-style** decoder: RMSNorm, rotary position embeddings (RoPE), SwiGLU MLP, no biases,
tied input/output embeddings. Size: 8 layers, 6 heads (head dim 64), dim 384, MLP hidden 1024
(Llama's 8/3 ratio), context 256: **15.7M parameters**, of which 1.6M are the embedding table.
The same block design as Llama and SmolLM, so M7 can load a real model.

Amended 2026-10-13 (M1): the first draft said dim 288 / 6 layers / hidden 768 would be ~15M. That shape
comes from llama2.c, where a 32,000-token vocabulary alone is 9.2M parameters; with our 4096-token
vocabulary it is only 7.2M. A test on the parameter count caught it. We spent the freed budget on width
and depth instead. Amended in place rather than in a new ADR, because nothing had been built on the old
shape yet.

**Engine:** plain Rust, `f32` math, no ML framework. Weights in **safetensors** (a JSON header plus raw
tensors; simple to parse, no code execution on load, unlike pickle). Crates: `glasswing-engine` (all
logic, tested natively) and `glasswing-wasm` (thin wasm-bindgen layer).

**Training:** PyTorch with CUDA, managed by uv in `train/`. PyTorch is the reference implementation:
the Rust engine is correct when it matches PyTorch on the golden fixtures.

## Consequences

- Correctness has a hard definition (parity with PyTorch to 1e-4), checked in CI, like the eval gate
  in Night Sky Digest.
- The model can only write children's stories. That is the point: its behaviour is legible.
- f32 weights for 15.7M parameters are ~63 MB; the browser needs f16 or int8 (M4).
- Any change to data, architecture or engine stack needs a new ADR.
